note: Lafayette's budget.json is built from these City documents alone (src/data/lafayette/build.ts, #59). Tables are read line by line from each page's extracted text (source/excerpts/{source}.json, PDF page numbers) and tied to their own totals. Two pages of the FY 2026-27 budget are printed as images with no text: the five-year forecast (PDF 17) and the capital program summary (PDF 21). Their rows under 'scans' are our reading of the rendered page, served from public/ at 'image'; no text check can confirm them, so each receipt says so, and the build ties every row to the table's own totals and to the text pages that repeat its figures. The budget's tables keep the heading 'Proposed Budget', though the Council adopted it on June 22, 2026 with four amendments, which the book includes; the City Manager's memo (PDF 7-12) is dated June 8, before them.

notes.caveat: Figures are from the City of Lafayette's FY 2026-27 budget, adopted June 22, 2026 (its tables keep the heading 'Proposed Budget'), and its audited financial report. Years before FY 2026-27 are shown for context, and years after it are the City's forecast. Not for investment-decision use.

reserveNotes.text: The City has said the drop in its reserves is on purpose. Last year's Final Budget called it “intentional and strategic”, a shift from building up reserves toward reinvesting in City facilities while keeping the reserve above its minimum.

cites.quote: Importantly, the reduction in reserves reflected in the Final Budget is intentional and strategic.
the Final Budget reflects a shift from reserve accumulation toward reinvestment in critical City facilities while still maintaining the 60% threshold.

glossary.definition: The City’s primary operating fund. It accounts for all financial resources of the general government, except those required to be accounted for in another fund.
glossary.quote: primary operating fund. It accounts for all financial resources of the general government, except those required to be accounted for in another fund.

glossary.definition: A half-cent sales tax Lafayette voters approved in November 2024. In the City’s words: “In November 2024 voters approved Measure H -- a 1/2 cent sales tax -- to support ongoing City programs. The additional sales tax was effective on April 1, 2025 and will continue for 7 years until March 30, 2032.”
glossary.quote: In November 2024 voters approved Measure H -- a 1/2 cent sales tax -- to support ongoing City programs. The additional sales tax was effective on April 1, 2025 and will continue for 7 years until March 30, 2032.

glossary.definition: Money the City sets aside year by year for a known future cost. The City’s financial report describes “sinking funds” for future operating costs such as vehicle replacements, vacation accruals, retiree healthcare, capital expenditures, deferred maintenance, and other monies that have been earmarked for specific purposes by the Council.
